findings.summary: The overlay panel draws only the two codes' solved flux — green imas-efit and blue nova contours, plus the black limiter ring — and no reference field. A colour census of the rendered 1400x1400 PNG finds exactly three non-white families (green rgb(46,146,88), blue rgb(31,95,168), black) with no third contour set, and panel.py's payload carries only psi_nova and psi_efit, no reference flux and no generating null positions. The evidence fragment's caption and alt text nevertheless say 'the reference flux as lines' and 'both codes' solved flux and the reference', and the paragraph above tells the reader the panel shows 'how far each code's nulls stand from the generating ones', which is data the rendered figure does not carry. A reader is told to make a comparison the panel cannot support.

The caption states that imas-efit's axis and X-point are 'marked open', but the rendered PNG shows both efit markers filled: a solid green square around the blue triangle at the magnetic axis, and a solid green plus behind the blue X at the saddle. A pixel map of the axis region shows the square solid green from edge to edge, and paint.py's draw_nulls call passes no face, so nova.media.poloidal draw_nulls sets markerfacecolor to the code colour for both codes. Because both sets are filled, fill does not distinguish them as the caption says; only shape does, and the two plus/X marks overlap along their arms at the saddle, so the small separation between the codes' nulls is hard to read.

The contour line widths invert the figure's emphasis: the subject, nova, is drawn at linewidth 0.9 while the comparison, imas-efit, is drawn at 1.6, so the code the panel is set against carries the heavier stroke. Drawing the subject thinner than what it is compared against works against the house rule that the subject takes the visual weight, and in the crowded core the thicker green contours partly mask the blue ones.

notes: Read-only figure review of the three rendered PNGs attached to this run. Only image-0.png, image-1.png and image-2.png were opened, plus pixel crops and colour measurements of those same PNGs; no SVG and no other image was opened, and no file was edited, created, moved, deleted, redrawn, relabelled or reformatted. The caption text was read from docs/evidence/fragments/inverse-equilibrium-baseline/drift-sequences-fit-iteration.html at the reviewed head only to check it against the rendered figure. The attachment order does not match the run manifest's figure list order: the first attachment renders imas-efit and the second renders nova, which was established from the rendered trace colours and y ranges rather than assumed. No suite runs for a figure review.

rubric_items.contrast: pass for all three: axis, tick and legend text is near-black on white in every PNG; the grey #929292 control trace in the two axis-error panels measures rgb(146,146,146), about 3.1:1 against white, clearing the 3:1 data-mark floor.
rubric_items.data_ink: pass for all three: the axis-error panels carry two 2.4-3.0 pt traces and one two-entry legend; the overlay carries 12 line contours per code plus the limiter ring and four null marks; no area fill, gradient or shaded band appears in any of the three PNGs.
rubric_items.decoration: pass for all three: background is pure white, the axis-error panels have no gridlines and no top or right spine, and the overlay has its axis off entirely with no grid or frame.
rubric_items.label_collision: pass for all three: in the axis-error panels the legend sits in the reserved strip above the axes and the y axis label clears the canvas edge; the overlay carries no axis labels, and its two plotted figures measured 1400x720 and 1400x1400 with no text touching a data mark, so nothing is clipped or overlapped.
rubric_items.legibility: pass for all three: the two axis-error PNGs (1400x720) each carry one 14 in panel with 16 pt axis labels 'axis error [mm]' and 'slice' and 14 pt ticks and legend over a 0-70 mm and a 0-42 mm scale, readable at a glance; the overlay (1400x1400) draws the contour map and vessel clearly, and the two codes' null markers stay distinguishable by shape (triangle/square, X/plus) where they nearly coincide.
rubric_items.table_form: pass for all three: the two axis-error panels are per-slice time series and the overlay is a spatial flux comparison, neither of which reduces to a table without losing the shape the reader needs.
